name: Finding Adjacent Duplicates in a Sequence of Numbers
description: Construct a program that checks whether a sequence of numbers, entered one at a time, contains adjacent duplicates. The user enters -1 to indicate the end of the input.\nFor example, 4 is a duplicate in the sequence of numbers 1, 3, 4, 4, -1.
code:
#Step 1: Read the first number that the user enters
text = input("Enter a number: ")
num = float(text)
#Step 2: Read the rest of the numbers that the user enters and check for adjacent duplicates
while num != -1 :
    previous = num
    text = input("Enter a number: ")
    num = float(text)    
    if num == previous :
        print("Duplicate input for number:", num)

1.content: #Step 1: Read the first number that the user enters

commentList: We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the first number. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its float representation because the number could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float().
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value.

4.content: #Step 2: Read the rest of the numbers that the user enters and check for adjacent duplicates

commentList: We need to repeat receiving the numbers from the user as long as the user enters a number that is different from -1. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input number is different from -1.
The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters a number that is different from -1. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters -1.
We store the number that the user entered in a variable called previous because we want to later compare it with the next number that user will enter to check if they are adjacent duplicate.

We need to read and process the next number that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the next number. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its float representation because the number could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float().
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value.
We check whether the number that the user entered is the duplicate of the previous number that the user entered. To determine if the two numbers are duplicate we need to test whether they are equal.
If the number that the user entered is equal to the previous number that was entered, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Duplicate input for number:" and the value of variable num.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
